mainTopic: Why making a stolen animal הקדש is not a 'sale', and רבי שמעון's rule on stealing קדשים
overview: The גמרא looks at a line in the משנה: a thief who stole an animal, made it הקדש, and then slaughtered or sold it pays כפל but not ארבעה וחמשה. It agrees the later slaughter can't make him pay, since by then the animal belonged to הקדש. But it asks why making the animal הקדש isn't itself a 'sale'. Two answers, one based on רבי שמעון and one based on רבי יוסי הגלילי, are tried and rejected. The final answer is that making something הקדש never counts as a sale: after a sale ראובן's ox becomes שמעון's, but after making it הקדש it is still called ראובן's ox. Next the גמרא asks why רבי שמעון's rule in the משנה seems backwards. It answers that he is talking about a different case: stealing animals that were already קדשים, which the פסוק 'וגנב מבית האיש' covers only when the owner must replace them. Finally it asks how a slaughter of קדשים can count for רבי שמעון, who holds that an unfit slaughter is not a slaughter. רבי יוחנן's answer comes in two versions: רב דימי says the thief slaughtered properly inside for the owner and the blood spilled, while רבין says he slaughtered inside but not for the owner.

steps.title: Closing words of the previous discussion: the extra part of the double payment
steps.stepSummary: The last words of the earlier discussion, pointing to the payment of the extra part of כפל.
steps.whatsHappening: These two words finish a sentence that began earlier in the גמרא. They wrap up the previous discussion before a new topic starts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase refers to the extra part of the כפל payment, meaning the amount beyond the קרן (the value of what was stolen). Nothing new is argued here; it only closes the earlier line of thought.

keyTerms.meaning: Payment
Double payment: a thief pays back twice the value of what he stole
The principal: the basic value of the stolen item

steps.confusionAlert: Don't try to read these words as the start of the new topic. They finish the sentence before them, and the new topic begins with גנב והקדיש.

phrases.english: The payment of the double payment.
phrases.notes: This finishes the sentence before it. It means the extra part of כפל, beyond the value of the item itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the discussion from the previous page.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The earlier discussion ends by pointing to the payment of the extra part of כפל.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: stole, made it holy, then slaughtered or sold
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a thief who stole an animal, made it הקדש, and only then slaughtered or sold it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: If he stole, then made it holy, and afterward slaughtered or sold it, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is opening a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that in this case the thief pays כפל but not ארבעה וחמשה (four or five times the value). The order matters: the הקדש came first, and only then the slaughter or sale.

keyTerms.meaning: He stole
He made it holy, dedicating it to the בית המקדש
Slaughtered or sold: the acts that normally bring the four- or five-times payment
The four- or five-times payment for a thief who slaughters or sells a stolen sheep or ox

steps.whyThisMatters: Normally slaughtering or selling a stolen sheep or ox brings the extra four- or five-times payment. This case shows how הקדש changes that result.

phrases.english: If he stole and consecrated it
phrases.notes: The full משנה says he pays כפל but not the four- or five-times payment; the כו׳ hints at the rest.

phrases.english: and afterward slaughtered or sold it, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: גָּנַב וְהִקְדִּישׁ וְאַחַר כָּךְ טָבַח וּמָכַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the previous discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A thief who made a stolen animal הקדש and then slaughtered or sold it pays כפל but not ארבעה וחמשה.

steps.title: The slaughter makes sense, but why isn't making it holy like a sale?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that he isn't liable for the slaughter, but asks why making the animal הקדש doesn't count as selling it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: It makes sense that he is not liable for the slaughter, because when he slaughtered, he slaughtered an animal that belonged to הקדש, not one that belonged to its owner. But he should be liable for making it הקדש! What difference is there between selling it to a regular person and selling it to Heaven?
steps.whatsHappening: First the גמרא agrees with part of the משנה: the slaughter can't make him pay extra. Then it challenges the other part: the act of making the animal הקדש should count as a 'sale' and make him pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slaughter brings the extra payment only if he slaughtered the owner's animal, and by then it was הקדש property. But giving the animal to הקדש moves it out of his hands, just like a sale. So the act of making it הקדש should itself bring the four- or five-times payment.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense: grants one part before challenging another part
Slaughter
An ordinary person, not הקדש
To Heaven: giving it to הקדש

steps.confusionAlert: The בשלמא part is not the question. It is the part the גמרא agrees with. The real challenge starts at אלא.

phrases.english: They say: It makes sense
that for the slaughter he is not liable,
because when he slaughtered,
he slaughtered an animal of הקדש,
and he did not slaughter its owner's animal;
but for the consecration, he should be liable!
phrases.notes: He means the act of making it הקדש should itself bring the four- or five-times payment.

phrases.english: What difference is it to me if he sold it to an ordinary person,
or if he sold it to Heaven?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of the משנה just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that he pays no four- or five-times payment.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Making the animal הקדש moves it out of the thief's hands, just like a sale. So it should bring the four- or five-times payment.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי שמעון: such קדשים still belong to the owner
steps.stepSummary: The משנה follows רבי שמעון, who says קדשים the owner must replace are still treated as the owner's property, so making them הקדש is not a sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is רבי שמעון's, who said: קדשים that the owner must replace if lost are still in their owner's possession.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying which תנא the משנה follows. According to רבי שמעון, making the animal הקדש doesn't take it out of the thief's possession.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the owner must replace the animal when it is lost or dies (אחריות), רבי שמעון treats it as still his. So when the thief made it הקדש in this way, nothing left his possession, and it isn't like a sale. That is why the act of making it הקדש brings no four- or five-times payment.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this? Used to name the תנא behind a source
Animals made holy as offerings
Responsibility to replace the animal if it is lost or dies
In its owner's possession

steps.whatToRemember: This first answer says the משנה follows רבי שמעון: קדשים the owner must replace still count as his, so making them הקדש is not a 'sale'. Step 5 rejects this answer, and the final explanation comes in Step 8.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that whether making something הקדש counts as moving it out of one's possession can depend on whether the owner still carries responsibility for it.

phrases.english: Whose view is this?
It is רבי שמעון, who said:
Sacred animals that one must replace if lost
stand in the possession of their owner.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Names the תנא behind the משנה (whose view this is).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Making the animal הקדש is like selling it to Heaven, so it should bring the four- or five-times payment.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי שמעון, קדשים with אחריות stay in the owner's possession, so making them הקדש is not a sale.

steps.title: Only the later part of the משנה follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the answer that the משנה follows רבי שמעון. The later clause of the משנה names רבי שמעון, so the earlier clause must not be his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the later part of the משנה is the view of רבי שמעון, the earlier part must not be the view of רבי שמעון!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the answer from Step 4. The משנה only brings in רבי שמעון's name in its later part, so the first part, which is our case, cannot be his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 explained our case using רבי שמעון. But the משנה quotes רבי שמעון by name only in the סיפא. That suggests the רישא follows a different opinion, so that explanation no longer works for it.

keyTerms.meaning: The first or earlier clause of a משנה
The last or later clause of a משנה
'But from the fact that...'; it introduces an inference used to push back

phrases.english: But from the fact that the latter clause is Rabbi Shimon,
it follows that the first clause is not Rabbi Shimon!

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the רישא of the משנה follows רבי שמעון
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה names רבי שמעון only in the סיפא, which implies the רישא is someone else's view

steps.title: The משנה is about lesser offerings, following רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new answer. The thief made the animal קדשים קלים, and according to רבי יוסי הגלילי those still belong to the owner, so making them הקדש is not a sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what case are we dealing with? קדשים קלים, following רבי יוסי הגלילי, who says קדשים קלים are the owner's property and stay in his possession.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new explanation to replace the rejected one. It says our case is about an animal made into a קדשים קלים offering, following רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Paying ארבעה וחמשה needs the animal to leave the thief's possession, as in a sale. רבי יוסי הגלילי holds that קדשים קלים are still the owner's property. So making the animal הקדש this way does not take it out of his hands, and it is not a sale.

keyTerms.meaning: 'With what case are we dealing here?'; the גמרא narrows the case to fit the משנה
Offerings of lesser holiness, such as a שלמים
The owner's property
They stand in his possession

phrases.english: Rather, with what are we dealing here?
With offerings of lesser sanctity,
phrases.notes: He means the thief made the stolen animal into this kind of offering.

phrases.english: and according to Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,
who says: offerings of lesser sanctity
are the property of the owner,
and they stand in his possession.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected רבי שמעון answer with a new explanation
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case together with assigning a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Making the animal הקדש takes it away from the thief, so it should count like a sale
steps.terutzMaskana: With קדשים קלים, according to רבי יוסי הגלילי, the animal stays the owner's property, so making it הקדש is not a sale

steps.title: Then the משנה should have taught the difference for most holy offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new answer. If קדשי קדשים would make the thief pay ארבעה וחמשה, the משנה should have taught that difference inside our own case, instead of teaching a separate case in the earlier clause.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about קדשי קדשים? Would he pay ארבעה וחמשה? Then instead of teaching earlier 'he stole, slaughtered, and then made it הקדש: he pays ארבעה וחמשה,' the משנה should have made the split in this case itself: 'When is this said? With קדשים קלים. But with קדשי קדשים he pays ארבעה וחמשה!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 6. If the exemption only covers קדשים קלים, the משנה should have taught the opposite ruling for קדשי קדשים right inside this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 means that with קדשי קדשים, making the animal הקדש would count as a sale, so he would pay ארבעה וחמשה. If so, the משנה had a ready case of paying inside this same situation. Instead it taught a separate case, 'stole, slaughtered, then made it הקדש,' which suggests the משנה did not intend any split.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings of the highest holiness, such as an עולה or חטאת
The fourfold or fivefold payment for stealing and then slaughtering or selling a sheep or ox
'Rather than teaching...'
'Let him split and teach within the same case'
'In what case are these words said?'; it introduces a limit on a ruling

steps.confusionAlert: The 'earlier clause' (רישא) here is a different case, where he slaughtered first and only then made the animal הקדש. Do not mix it up with our case, where he made it הקדש first.

phrases.english: But with offerings of the most sacred order, what?
He pays the fourfold or fivefold payment?!
phrases.notes: This follows from Step 6: those offerings are not the owner's property, so making them הקדש would work like a sale.

phrases.english: Rather than teaching in the earlier clause:
He stole and slaughtered and afterward consecrated,
he pays the fourfold or fivefold payment;
let him distinguish and teach within the case itself:
In what case are these words said?
With offerings of lesser sanctity,
but with offerings of the most sacred order
he pays the fourfold or fivefold payment!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the קדשים קלים answer of Step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that our case is limited to קדשים קלים according to רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If קדשי קדשים would make the thief liable, the משנה should have taught that split within this case, instead of using a different case (slaughtered, then made הקדש) to show when he pays

steps.title: Making an animal holy is not a sale, whatever kind of offering it becomes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the difference between קדשי קדשים and קדשים קלים. Making the animal הקדש never counts as a sale, because the ox does not pass to a new owner the way it does in a real sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it makes no difference whether it is קדשי קדשים or קדשים קלים. And as for your question, 'What's the difference between selling it to a person and selling it to Heaven?': when he sells it to a person, first it was ראובן's ox and now it is שמעון's ox. When he 'sells' it to Heaven, first it was ראובן's ox and now it is still ראובן's ox.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a brand-new answer to the original question from Step 3. Making the animal הקדש is simply not the kind of transfer that counts as selling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 attacked the answer that split קדשי קדשים from קדשים קלים, so the גמרא drops that split completely. The new idea is that a sale means the ox passes from one person to another, ראובן to שמעון. Making it הקדש does not hand it to a new person in that way, so the thief does not pay ארבעה וחמשה for it.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually / really. Signals a fresh answer that drops the earlier approach
It makes no difference
An ordinary person (as opposed to הקדש / Heaven)
He 'sold' it to Heaven, meaning he made it הקדש
At first... and now

steps.confusionAlert: ראובן and שמעון here are just sample names, like 'John and Bob.' This שמעון is NOT רבי שמעון from the משנה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic idea for the rest of the sugya: a real 'sale' means a change of owner, and making something הקדש is not treated that way.

phrases.english: Rather, actually,
it makes no difference if it is offerings of the most holy kind
and it makes no difference if it is offerings of lesser holiness;
phrases.notes: So the split from Step 6, which Step 7 attacked, is being dropped completely.

phrases.english: and as for what was hard for you:
phrases.notes: This points back to the question in Step 3.

phrases.english: what difference is it to me if he sold it to an ordinary person
or if he sold it to Heaven?
If he sold it to an ordinary person,
at first it was Reuven's ox,
and now it is Shimon's ox.
If he sold it to Heaven,
at first it was Reuven's ox,
and now it is still Reuven's ox.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְעוֹלָם לָא שְׁנָא קׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives up the answer that Step 7 attacked and answers Step 3's question in a new way.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Conceptual distinction: a sale changes the owner, but making something הקדש does not
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Making the animal הקדש is just like selling it, so the thief should pay ארבעה וחמשה
steps.terutzMaskana: Making it הקדש is not a sale because the ox does not pass to a new owner, for every kind of קדשים

steps.title: רבי שמעון's rule looks backwards
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון in the משנה. Even if he holds that making an animal הקדש is like selling it, his rule should have been the opposite of what the משנה says.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'רבי שמעון says, etc.' They say: Fine, רבי שמעון holds 'What's the difference between selling it to a person and selling it to Heaven?' But then he should have said the opposite!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new section on רבי שמעון's words in the משנה. It raises a problem with them, and the next step spells the problem out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי שמעון makes the thief pay ארבעה וחמשה for קדשים the owner must replace, and exempts him for קדשים he need not replace. The גמרא assumes that for רבי שמעון the payment comes from making the animal הקדש, which he treats like a sale. If so, the גמרא says, his two rulings seem to be switched.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted that / even if we accept that
He should have said the opposite
Etc. Shows that only the opening words of the משנה are quoted

steps.confusionAlert: This is a different question from Step 8. Step 8 was about the earlier part of the משנה, where making it הקדש is not a sale. Here we are asking about רבי שמעון, who is assumed to treat it like a sale.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says, etc.
phrases.notes: Only the opening words are quoted. The full line in the משנה separates קדשים the owner must replace from ones he need not replace.

phrases.english: They say:
Granted that Rabbi Shimon holds:
what difference is it to me if he sold it to an ordinary person
or if he sold it to Heaven;
he should have said the opposite:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the earlier part of the משנה to רבי שמעון's part, and raises a new problem there.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's rule in the משנה: liable for קדשים the owner must replace, exempt for ones he need not replace
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If making it הקדש counts as a sale, the case where the animal truly leaves the owner should be the one that costs the thief, and that is the opposite of רבי שמעון's rule

steps.title: Spelling out the reversed rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains what 'the opposite' means. If the owner must replace the animal, it never left him, so the thief should be exempt. If he need not replace it, it fully left him, so the thief should be liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Offerings he must replace: he should be exempt, because the animal has not yet left his possession. Offerings he need not replace: he should be liable, because he has removed the animal from his possession!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge from Step 9 by showing exactly how רבי שמעון's rule 'should' have looked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With קדשים he must replace, the owner still carries responsibility, so the animal is still treated as his and nothing was really 'sold.' With קדשים he need not replace, the animal has fully left him, which looks like a real sale and should bring ארבעה וחמשה. So the logic of a sale points the exact opposite way from the משנה. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: Responsibility to replace a lost or dead offering
Possession / ownership
Still / not yet
Exempt / liable (here, for ארבעה וחמשה)

steps.whyThisMatters: This ties the idea of 'sale' to 'leaving one's possession,' and the answer to רבי שמעון will have to explain why his rule doesn't follow this logic.

phrases.english: Offerings that he is responsible to replace,
he should be exempt,
phrases.notes: Exempt from paying ארבעה וחמשה. The ruling in the משנה is the reverse.

phrases.english: because it has not yet left his possession;
offerings that he is not responsible to replace,
he should be liable,
because he has removed it from his possession!

steps.triggerLanguage: קֳדָשִׁים שֶׁחַיָּיב בְּאַחְרָיוּתָן פָּטוּר דְּאַכַּתִּי לָא נְפַק מֵרְשׁוּתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the 'opposite' rule that Step 9 said רבי שמעון should have taught.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's split between קדשים the owner must replace and ones he need not replace
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Responsibility to replace means the animal is still in his possession, so it is not a sale. No responsibility means it fully left him, which is a sale. So liability should go the opposite way from the משנה.

steps.title: רבי שמעון is talking about a different case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from steps 9-10: רבי שמעון's words are not about whether making an animal הקדש is like selling it. He is talking about another case.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: רבי שמעון is talking about a different matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge against רבי שמעון by saying his words belong to a different case. This line sets up the next step, where the גמרא shows which case that is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed רבי שמעון was saying whether making the animal הקדש counts as a sale. If he is not talking about that at all, his rule cannot be 'backwards.' The challenge falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: He is referring to a different matter

phrases.english: They say: Rabbi Shimon –
is referring to a different matter,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אַמִּילְּתָא אַחֲרִיתִי קָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 9-10 that רבי שמעון's rule seems backwards.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the subject of the statement: רבי שמעון is talking about a different case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון was ruling on whether making a stolen animal הקדש counts as selling it.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון is ruling on a separate case that the משנה has in mind, so the challenge does not apply.

steps.title: How the משנה should be read
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the משנה's meaning. One who steals from a thief does not pay four and five. Likewise, one who steals הקדש from the owner's house is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the משנה means: someone who steals from a thief does not pay four or five times. Likewise, someone who steals הקדש from its owner's house is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the 'different case' it just mentioned. It reads the משנה as also including a case of stealing an animal that is already הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With 'והכי קתני' the גמרא reads both rulings into the משנה as its intended meaning. The second ruling, stealing הקדש from the owner's house, is the case that רבי שמעון is reacting to. In this case the animal was already הקדש before the theft, so this is not the earlier case of a thief who makes the animal הקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what it teaches (how to read the משנה)
One who steals from a thief
The four-times and five-times payment for slaughtering or selling a stolen sheep or ox
Property belonging to the בית המקדש
The owner

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with the earlier case. There, the thief made the animal הקדש after stealing it. Here, the animal was already הקדש before it was stolen.

phrases.english: And this is what it teaches:
One who steals after a thief
does not pay the fourfold and fivefold payment,
and likewise, one who steals consecrated property
from the owner's house is exempt.
phrases.notes: This is the piece the משנה doesn't say openly, but the גמרא says it is meant.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the 'different matter' that step 11 said רבי שמעון is talking about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who steals from a thief does not pay four and five. One who steals הקדש from its owner's house is also exempt.

steps.title: The verse says from the house of the man
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the source for exempting a thief of הקדש: the פסוק says 'from the house of the man,' and not from הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why? The פסוק says 'and it was stolen from the house of the man,' and not from הקדש's house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why stealing הקדש is exempt, and answers with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra payments a thief owes apply only when he steals from a person ('the man'). הקדש belongs to the בית המקדש, not to a person, so those payments do not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
From the house of the man, meaning from a private person

phrases.english: What is the reason?
"And it was stolen from the house of the man" –
and not from the house of הקדש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the rule in step 12 that a thief of הקדש is exempt.
steps.raayaObject: The exemption for one who steals הקדש.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות 22:6: 'וְגֻנַּב מִבֵּית הָאִישׁ' teaches 'from a person,' not from הקדש.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: it depends on whether the owner must replace it
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון rules that if the owner must replace the קדשים, the thief is liable, because they still count as 'from the house of the man.' If the owner need not replace them, the thief is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: if the owner is responsible to replace the קדשים, the thief is liable, because they are still 'from the house of the man.' If the owner is not responsible, the thief is exempt, because they are not 'from the house of the man.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives רבי שמעון's view on stealing הקדש. This is the 'different matter' he was talking about all along.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the owner must bring a replacement, losing the animal is the owner's loss, so it still counts as his. If he need not replace it, it belongs only to הקדש. This explains the ruling that seemed 'backwards' in steps 9-10: it was never about selling.

keyTerms.meaning: Animals set aside as קרבנות
Responsible for them: the owner must replace them if they are lost
We can apply the פסוק's words to this case
Liable (must pay)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון's rule is about stealing animals that are already קדשים, not about a thief who makes an animal הקדש. If the owner must replace them, they are still 'his,' so the thief pays. If not, the thief is exempt.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answers the challenge of steps 9-10 and keeps the reading of the משנה from step 8: making the animal הקדש is not a sale.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
Sacrificial animals that he is responsible for –
phrases.notes: He means the owner must bring another animal if this one is lost or stolen.

phrases.english: he is liable.
What is the reason?
We apply to it: "and it was stolen from the house of the man."
And those he is not responsible for –
he is exempt,
because we do not apply to it:
"and it was stolen from the house of the man."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: קֳדָשִׁים שֶׁחַיָּיב בְּאַחְרָיוּתָן חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי שמעון's disagreement with the rule in step 12, using the same פסוק from step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A thief who steals קדשים the owner must replace is liable. If the owner need not replace them, the thief is exempt.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי שמעון's rule is about whether stolen קדשים still count as the owner's, not about whether making an animal הקדש is a sale. This answers the challenge of steps 9-10.

steps.title: An unfit slaughter is not a slaughter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון's ruling. He holds elsewhere that an unfit slaughter does not count as slaughter, and slaughtering stolen קדשים looks like an unfit slaughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, we know that רבי שמעון said: a slaughter that is not fit is not called a slaughter. Slaughtering קדשים is also a slaughter that is not fit! So how can the thief pay four and five?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי שמעון's ruling from step 14 by pointing to another rule of his. If his slaughter 'doesn't count,' the thief should never pay four and five.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Paying four and five requires stealing and then slaughtering or selling. רבי שמעון holds that a slaughter which does not make the meat permitted is not a real slaughter. Slaughtering קדשים normally does not permit the meat, so the thief has not really 'slaughtered,' and he should not pay four and five.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, since (opens a challenge built on something we already know)
A slaughter that is not fit, meaning it does not make the meat permitted to eat
It is not called a slaughter, so it does not count as one
Animals set aside as sacrifices

steps.confusionAlert: This challenge is not saying the thief did nothing wrong. It only asks whether the slaughter counts for the extra penalty of four and five.

phrases.english: Now, we have heard regarding רבי שמעון
that he said: a slaughter that is not fit
is not called a slaughter;

phrases.aramaic: קֳדָשִׁים נָמֵי שְׁחִיטָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ רְאוּיָה הִיא!
phrases.english: sacrificial animals too, it is a slaughter that is not fit!
phrases.notes: A sacrifice slaughtered outside the בית המקדש can't be eaten, so it is an 'unfit' slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי שמעון's ruling in step 14 using his own rule from elsewhere.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's ruling that a thief of קדשים the owner must replace pays four and five
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Internal contradiction: רבי שמעון holds that an unfit slaughter is not a slaughter, and slaughtering קדשים is unfit, so the thief should be exempt.

steps.title: The thief slaughtered it properly inside for the owner
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי quotes רבי יוחנן: the case is where the thief slaughtered an unblemished animal inside the עזרה for the owner's sake, so the slaughter is fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the case is where the thief slaughtered unblemished animals inside, for the sake of the owner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by placing רבי שמעון's ruling in a case where slaughtering the קדשים is a proper, fit slaughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the animal is unblemished, slaughtered in the right place, and slaughtered for its owner, it is a proper sacrifice and the meat may be eaten. That makes it a fit slaughter, so even רבי שמעון agrees it counts.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (an אמורא bringing a teaching from ארץ ישראל)
Unblemished animals, fit to be offered
Inside, in the עזרה of the בית המקדש
For the sake of the owner, on his behalf

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came
he said that Rabbi Yochanan says:
it is where he slaughters unblemished animals inside
phrases.notes: 'Inside' means in the Temple courtyard, the proper place for slaughtering sacrifices.

phrases.english: for the sake of the owner.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every slaughter of stolen קדשים is unfit, so רבי שמעון could not make the thief liable.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is a valid sacrificial slaughter, unblemished, inside, for the owner, so the slaughter is fit and counts.

steps.title: But the animal went back to its owner
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to רב דימי's case: if the thief offered the sacrifice for the owner, the owner got his animal back.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then the principal has returned to the owner!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב דימי's answer. If the sacrifice was offered for the owner, he got what he wanted from it, so why should the thief pay four and five?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner set the animal aside as his sacrifice, and the thief offered it for him. That is like giving the stolen item back, and once it is back there is no penalty of four and five.

keyTerms.meaning: But look (opens an objection)
The principal, the stolen item itself
It returned

phrases.english: But the principal has returned to the owner!
phrases.notes: 'Principal' here means the animal itself. The owner's sacrifice was offered for him, so it is as if he got it back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the case set up in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי's case of slaughtering inside for the owner
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Offering the sacrifice on the owner's behalf amounts to returning the stolen animal, which should cancel four and five.

steps.title: The blood spilled
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בר אבין answers that the blood spilled before it reached the מזבח, so the owner got nothing from the sacrifice.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר אבין said: the case is where the blood spilled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes רב דימי's case so it is not like returning the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The slaughter was still proper, so it counts as a fit slaughter. But since the blood spilled before it was put on the מזבח, the sacrifice did not work for the owner. He gained nothing, so the animal was not 'returned' to him.

keyTerms.meaning: The blood spilled, before it could be placed on the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: In רב דימי's version, the thief is liable when he slaughters properly, inside and for the owner, but the blood spills, so the owner gets no benefit.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Avin said:
where the blood was spilled.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר אָבִין שֶׁנִּשְׁפַּךְ הַדָּם
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Offering the sacrifice for the owner gives him back his animal.
steps.terutzMaskana: The blood spilled, so the owner got no atonement and nothing was returned, while the slaughter itself was still fit.

steps.title: רבין's version: slaughtered inside, not for the owner
steps.stepSummary: רבין quotes רבי יוחנן differently: the thief slaughtered an unblemished animal inside, but not for the owner's sake.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the case is where the thief slaughtered unblemished animals inside, not for the sake of the owner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second report of רבי יוחנן's answer to the challenge in step 15. This version avoids the 'returned to the owner' problem from the start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slaughtered inside and unblemished, the meat may be eaten, so the slaughter is fit and counts. Because it was not done for the owner, he does not fulfill his obligation with it, so nothing was returned to him. No spilled blood is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Not for the sake of the owner

steps.whatToRemember: Two versions of רבי יוחנן: רב דימי says the thief slaughtered for the owner, and the blood spilled. רבין says the thief slaughtered not for the owner. Both make the slaughter fit without returning anything to the owner.
steps.confusionAlert: רבין is not arguing with the question in step 15. He gives a different version of the same answer, so the objection in step 17 never comes up.

phrases.english: When Ravin came
he said that Rabbi Yochanan says:
it is where he slaughters unblemished animals inside
not for the sake of the owner.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the answer to step 15, as an alternative to רב דימי's version in steps 16 to 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A proper slaughter must be for the owner, which would return the animal to him.
steps.terutzMaskana: Slaughtered inside but not for the owner, the meat is permitted, so the slaughter is fit, and the owner gains nothing, so nothing was returned.
